bearings.paper_claim: Neuroticism was the only trait significant in the regression in both experiments. Exp 1: condition x N b = .45, p = .02 (minus sign lost in text extraction; authors describe a negative effect), interaction DR2 = .06, F(11,115) = 1.96, p = .04; under high pressure N b = .50, p < .01; under low pressure ns. Exp 2 (social plus time pressure, no low-pressure arm): N b = .31, p < .05; A b = .36, p < .01; model R2 = .19. Exp 1 agreeableness interaction only a trend, b = .33, p = .08. Authors call the agreeableness result exploratory.
bearings.system_side: The susceptibility composite weights A at .40 and N at .30 (comment: 'A ranked above N per the user's framing'). The docstring says high A adds to N-driven choking 'under social pressure (their Exp-2 interaction)'. Exp 2 has no low-pressure arm, so it cannot show an interaction. The default behavioural basis fills the A slot with cooperation_v2 (share-based; code comment gives rho +0.888 with bpf), not trait agreeableness. susc drives susc_mult [0.70, 1.30] and edge_mult [0.80, 1.20].

bearings.transfer_conditions: Weak transfer. (1) Construct: the outcome is worse choices on a delayed-reward lab task, not being moved by a persuader. (2) Population: undergraduates earning course credit at one university, individual decisions, an $8 bonus; not legislators facing lobbyists. (3) Measurement: the paper uses self-report BFI; the system uses text or behavioural proxies (affective_n for N, cooperation_v2 for A). (4) Size: Exp 1 step-1 R2 = .10 (condition plus five traits); the interaction increment is DR2 = .06, so the paper gives no anchor for the plus or minus 30 percent multiplier range. The paper supports the direction of an N-under-pressure term only; it does not support A outweighing N or the size of the term.
bearings.verifier_note: Every paper number checked against the text (Sections 2.2.3, 3.2.2, Tables 3 and 5). Softened: the 6 percent figure is the interaction increment DR2 only, not the trait effect; the 'strongest trait N gets smaller weight than weakest positive trait A' wording is muddled, since in Exp 2 A b = .36 exceeds N b = .31 and A is labelled exploratory. Negative sign of b = .45 cannot be confirmed from the extracted text. Code lines confirmed.

bearings.paper_claim: Under high pressure conscientiousness correlated negatively with performance, r = .27, p < .05 (Exp 1 correlation only). In the Exp 1 regression it was a trend, b = .16, p = .09. Experiment 2 found C not predictive: r = .16 ns, and Table 5 gives b = .16 with no significance mark. Authors say no clear conclusion about conscientiousness is possible. Extraversion and openness had no effect in either experiment.

bearings.system_side: The composite subtracts .20 x C and .10 x E, so high-C and high-E members count as less susceptible (lines 186 and 189). The docstring at lines 9-10 says these dampeners are design priors, not Byrne findings.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The paper's C direction is opposite to the code's dampener sign, but the only evidence is one uncontrolled correlation that the authors decline to interpret and that did not replicate. That qualifies the term; it does not contradict it. For C and E, the honest wording is that this paper gives no support to the dampener.

bearings.paper_claim: The paper explains N-driven choking by working memory: pressure and anxiety use up working memory, so neurotic people take the immediate reward. The authors measured no anxiety, mood or working-memory capacity and ran no pressure manipulation check. Self-rated importance did not differ by condition (Low M = 4.68, SD 2.42; High M = 5.17, SD 2.14; ns).

bearings.paper_claim: The agreeableness result rests on self-report BFI agreeableness predicting worse task performance. It is exploratory and significant only in the uncontrolled Exp 2 (b = .36, p < .01). The paper has nothing on projected or communal rhetoric.

Systematic review of how Big Five traits moderate persuasion-strategy effects. That is the persuadability construct the receptivity layer needs, which Byrne's choking task does not measure.

Speech-based elite personality measurement. The lexical Big Five basis that fills the composite at receptivity_layer.py:189 comes from this family of measures; Byrne used the self-report BFI.

summary_issues: 'Its strongest trait (N) gets a smaller weight than its weakest positive trait (A)' is muddled. In Exp 2, A b = .36 exceeds N b = .31, and the authors label A exploratory. Better: N is the only pre-specified trait that replicated; A is exploratory and significant only in the uncontrolled Exp 2.

The summary's account of effect sizes is right, but bearing 1 said trait effects explain about 6 percent of variance. Correction: 6 percent is the interaction increment DR2 = .06; step-1 R2 = .10 (condition plus five traits).

The H5 result (n = 441, partial r = +0.036), genre-transfer rho .050/.161, and the adjective 'well-powered' are project claims, not paper claims. They were not re-derived in this check and the adjective is unsupported here.
The quoted audit phrase 'does not converge with comfort-curve' was not found in the Melange audits folder, so the quotation is unverified.

'Paul's position' and 'his notes are stale' are inferred from code docstring framing. No Paul annotation exists (n_annots = 0, paul_entries empty), so the attribution should read as code-comment framing, not Paul's stated position.

Experiment 2 N: the summary gives about 61 to 62 analysed. The regression df F(5,55) implies N = 61, and the paper does not reconcile this with excluding 3 of 65; the discrepancy is real and should be stated as unreconciled.
